Advanced degree (MA, MFA, or PhD) in art history, history of photography, visual studies, or a related discipline.
Other: Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends to support programs and exhibitions. - Ability to work collaboratively in a complex, multi-unit academic environment.

Minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional curatorial experience in a museum, academic gallery, or research collection, including at least six (6) years in a leadership, supervisory, or project-management capacity; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience in scholarly or curatorial focus on nineteenth- and twentieth-century photography and/or photographic modernism and its legacies.

Demonstrated advanced experience working with photographic collections of historical significance, including collections-based research, interpretation, and scholarly use. Proven ability to develop, manage, and interpret exhibitions drawn from historical photographic collections.
Experience working with rare or primary-source photographic materials, including early processes and archival collections.
Demonstrated experience supporting academic research, teaching, and curriculum-connected programs through direct engagement with original works of art.
Experience working in an academic museum or university-based collection with a strong teaching and research mission.
Experience contributing to grant-funded projects or external partnerships.

Demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, including the ability to engage critically with the histories of representation, power, and exclusion embedded in photographic collections, and to advance inclusive, ethical, and accessible approaches to collections care, exhibitions, research access, and programming.

Collection Management - Provide professional stewardship of the photographic collections in collaboration with the Senior Curator and Collections Manager. - Contribute to accessioning, cataloging, documentation, and intellectual organization of the collection in accordance with museum best practices and UC policies. - Participate in collections planning, including identifying priorities for acquisitions, deaccessions, and long-term care. - Conduct and support collections-based research, including provenance research, contextual analysis, and preparation of interpretive materials. - Facilitate access to the collections for internal and external researchers, coordinating study visits and responding to scholarly inquiries. - Contribute to collections-related grant proposals, reports, and compliance documentation as assigned. (30% time)

Student and Faculty Research & Exhibitions - Serve as a primary liaison between UCR ARTS and academic departments to support curricular use of the collections. - Collaborate with faculty to integrate collections-based research, print viewings, and exhibition projects into undergraduate and graduate coursework. - Mentor students in curatorial research, exhibition development, and professional museum practices. - Curate or co-curate exhibitions drawn from museum collections, including student- and faculty-driven projects, in collaboration with curators and exhibition staff. - Contribute to interpretive content for exhibitions and programs, including wall texts, publications, and digital resources. - Support the planning, interpretation, and installation of exhibitions, working closely with preparators, registrar, and collections staff. - Supervise and guide student employees, interns, and volunteers engaged in collections and exhibition activities. (30% time)

Academic and Public Programs - Working closely with the Director of Education and Public Programs, develop and organize academic programs that activate the collections, including lecture series, symposia, panel discussions, and visiting artist or scholar presentations. - Collaborate with campus partners to align programming with departmental curricula, research initiatives, and interdisciplinary priorities. - Participate in public engagement initiatives that extend the educational impact of the museum collections beyond the university. - Represent UCR ARTS in academic and professional contexts, as assigned. (30% time)

Additional Professional Responsibilities - Contribute to strategic planning for exhibitions, collections use, and academic initiatives in collaboration with UCR ARTS leadership. - Participate in departmental committees, working groups, and cross-unit initiatives related to collections, exhibitions, and academic engagement. - Assist with grant development, donor cultivation, and stewardship activities. - Contribute to assessment, reporting, and documentation of exhibitions and academic programs, including preparation of materials for internal review and external stakeholders. - Support communications and outreach efforts by providing content expertise for publications, websites, and promotional materials. - Stay current with developments in photographic scholarship, museum practice, and academic engagement, and apply this knowledge to ongoing work. Supervision and Collaboration - Receives general direction from the Senior Curator. - Works closely with Senior Curator, Director of Education and Public Programs, Head of Exhibitions, Collections Manager, Registrar, preparators, and education and communications staff. - May supervise Museum Scientists, student employees, interns, and volunteers on a project or ongoing basis. - Collaborates extensively with faculty, students, and campus partners. (10% time)
